description:
rfc8398.rs:380-411 emits Error detail strings like:

  'rfc822Name SAN entry alice@example.com is malformed for equivalence checking (no @ delimiter); RFC 8398 §3 presupposes well-formed RFC 5322 mailbox addresses'

The wording presupposes-well-formed-addresses is correct but reads as defensive after-the-fact justification. The user at 2am sees 'malformed for equivalence checking' and wonders whether the lint is broken or their cert is.

Cleaner shape:

  'SmtpUTF8Mailbox SAN entry contains no @ delimiter; RFC 5322 mailbox required (per RFC 8398 §3)'

The principle: the user wants to know what failed and what spec said it should. Two halves: (1) one-line factual description of the broken thing; (2) one-line spec pointer. The current 'presupposes well-formed addresses' wording adds defensive context that obscures both halves.

Minor — every error message in the codebase deserves a once-over for 2am-readability. Flagged because rfc8398's equivalence detail is the longest and most easily misread.
title: Rfc8398SmimeMailboxEquivalenceLint detail messages bury the spec citation
